record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the full compressible Euler equations of a polytropic fluid with spatially periodic boundary conditions, do global-in-time spatially periodic weak solutions exist, and what is their large-time asymptotic behavior? More specifically, are there examples with piecewise constant periodic initial data that cease to exist in finite time, or examples whose values decay to their average over each period with different rates in time?

evidence.quote: Spatial periodic solutions. In their fundamental work [25], Glimm and Lax obtained the existence and large time asymptotic behavior of spatial periodic solutions to the isentropic Euler equations.

the theory of global (in time) existence and large time asymptotic behavior of spatial periodic solutions to the full Euler equation for polytropic fluids remains completely open. ... Is there example of spatial periodic weak solution for the full Euler equation with piecewise constant periodic initial data which ceases to exist in finite time? Are there examples of special spatial periodic solutions which decay to their average values over each period with different rate of decay in time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the full compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid in one space dimension:
  ∂_t ρ + ∂_x(ρ u) = 0,
  ∂_t(ρ u) + ∂_x(ρ u^2 + p) = 0,
  ∂_t(ρ E) + ∂_x(ρ u E + p u) = 0,
where ρ ≥ 0 is the density, u is the velocity, E = e + u^2/2 is the specific total energy, e is the specific internal energy, and the pressure obeys the polytropic equation of state p = (γ−1) ρ e with adiabatic exponent γ > 1. Impose spatially periodic boundary conditions, i.e. seek solutions (ρ, u, e)(t, x) that are periodic in x with a fixed period L > 0, with periodic initial data (ρ_0, u_0, e_0) of bounded variation (or, more specifically, piecewise constant on each period).

Address the following:

(a) Do there exist global-in-time spatially periodic weak (entropy) solutions for arbitrary periodic initial data of bounded total variation? If so, describe their large-time asymptotic behavior as t → ∞.

(b) Construct, or prove the nonexistence of, an example of a spatially periodic weak solution arising from piecewise constant periodic initial data whose total variation (or some equivalent norm) blows up in finite time, so that the solution ceases to exist globally.

(c) Construct, or rule out, examples of special spatially periodic weak solutions that decay toward their spatial averages over each period as t → ∞ with rates of decay in t that differ among the conserved quantities (mass, momentum, energy).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any global existence and large-time asymptotic theory for spatially periodic weak solutions of the full (non-isentropic) compressible Euler equations for polytropic fluids. The classical Glimm–Lax periodic theory is limited to the isentropic case, and recent work on the full system focuses on damping/heat conduction, spherical symmetry, time-periodic smooth solutions, or special structural assumptions, none of which resolve the spatially periodic weak-solution question. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Global Solutions of the One-Dimensional Compressible Euler Equations with Nonlocal Interactions via the Inviscid Limit
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work focuses on isentropic 1D Euler with nonlocal interactions, not on the full polytropic system in periodic settings.
status_evidence.claim: Modern global existence results target the isentropic case rather than the full polytropic Euler system on a torus.

status_evidence.title: Global Existence and Long-Time Behavior of Solutions to the Full Compressible Euler Equations with Damping and Heat Conduction in R^3
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence for the full Euler system requires damping and heat conduction in this work.
status_evidence.claim: Available global results for the full Euler system rely on dissipative mechanisms not present in the pure polytropic Euler model.
